description: Pulverised concrete, asbestos from older buildings, lead from paint and pipes, and combustion products, inhaled by children playing in it for years after the fighting.
energy_note: A playground made of the building.

aspect: Lead exposure and neurodevelopment is not controversial
description: Unlike the prenatal-stress literature, the developmental effect of lead on IQ and attention is settled science. War reliably remobilises lead that was safely bound in structures.
energy_note: The least disputed mechanism in this whole file.

aspect: Nobody measures it, so nobody can claim for it
description: Environmental sampling requires a functioning state, which is precisely what is absent. Twenty years later there is no baseline data and therefore no basis for any compensation claim.

aspect: Water and sanitation failure has its own developmental cost
description: Repeated early-childhood diarrhoeal illness and chronic undernutrition produce stunting and cognitive effects independent of any direct war injury.
energy_note: Killed slowly by the plumbing, not the ordnance.
